newsitem.title: UK: European VGO firms with avails low, demand up.
newsitem.headline: European VGO firms with avails low, demand up.

text.p: European vacuum gas oil firmer by mid-week with a transatlantic arb completely open but few avails seen on the market and rising European demand, especially for barges.
Traders said few low sulphur VGO cargoes were on offer, and at least one seller was offering at the $126 mark for a July 10 loader, with sellers a few dollars lower.
One refiner however said he may have some material loading in mid-July with a price tag of $119 fob, but other traders said it was poorer quality material.

"Flat prices have improved, you also have VGO discounts coming into the States and the arb is open and the market is much tighter, there's more demand in Europe, so it (VGO) strengthened," a trader with a U.S. major said.
"There is good German demand for barges and there's demand from other European buyers," the trader added.
A refiner said there are very few cargoes available to go to the States, and there is also buying interest for low sulphur VGO in northern Europe.
A second seller said it was not offering any cargoes until mid-July, adding the VGO barge market was more attractive at the moment, with at least a $6 premium over the former.
"The German market is looking for tonnes but avails are low, especially on low sulphur (VGO)," he added.
Traders said high sulphur VGO cargoes were quiet at the moment and were assessed at some $6 to $7 below low sulphur.

Traders were mixed over low sulphur barges, with some saying it was around the $122/$123 fob mark while others put it at about $127. One trader said he sold 10,000 tonnes into Germany earlier this week at high quote, or about that latter level.
